output.reason: Diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot wound now showing surrounding erythema, swelling and tenderness — features of a possible diabetic foot infection that require hands-on assessment today (wound inspection and probing, depth/drainage assessment, and any indicated testing). Presence of pus, warmth, streaking or deeper involvement cannot be established by message, and a messaging-only plan cannot examine or debride the wound.
output.patientMessage: I recommend you be seen in person today — an urgent care, your diabetes/foot clinic or an emergency department if nothing else is available — for a hands-on look at this foot wound. In diabetes, a cut with spreading redness, swelling and tenderness can become a deeper infection quickly. Counsel can stay involved in this thread, but don't wait for a reply. Go to an emergency department now if you develop fever or chills, spreading redness or red streaks up the leg, pus, or the skin turns dusky or black. Stay off that foot as much as you can until you're seen.
differential: Wound-associated cellulitis of the foot at a skin-break entry point
Localized abscess or deeper soft-tissue/bone involvement beneath a plantar wound
Non-infectious inflammation/irritation around a healing cut

output.evidenceLimitations: Sources used are a public-domain consumer health summary and an agent-compiled emergency-department synthesis; neither is a telehealth protocol, a specialty diabetic-foot guideline, nor proof of this patient's severity class. Key examination features (warmth, drainage, wound depth, streaking) and all measurements are unreported, so severity cannot be graded remotely; the routing rests on the reported findings plus diabetes.

citations.limitation: Consumer summary; advises prompt provider contact but does not specify care setting, urgency interval or treatment.
